To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the longitudinal variation of dB/dt along a Rutherford cable induces super coupling currents which can be characterised in terms of a characteristic length, characteristic time and a propagation velocity of the effect.
the longitudinal nonhomogeneity of dB/dt induces a longitudinal variation of the current in a Rutherford cable.

the super coupling currents in Rutherfords can be characterized by the characteristic length and time, and the propagation velocity, and that the characteristic length and velocity increase, and the characteristic time decreases with increasing contact resistance between strands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the measurement of the contact resistance of superconducting strands and the contact resistance of the strand matrix in Rutherford type cables.
the development of a new type of accelerator magnet, which can be produced at a reasonable price, but still fulfils the requirements of high gradient and high field quality.
the study of the effect of longitudinal nonhomogeneites in dB/dt on the super current distribution in Rutherford type cables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a longitudinal nonhomogeneous current in a Rutherford type of cable is always present.
the SCCs in accelerator magnets are not yet fully understood.
the nonhomogeneous current distributions induced by the field sweeps in accelerator magnets are very small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an accurate method to calculate the super coupling currents (and the corresponding characteristic length, time, and velocity) in Rutherford cables.
the effect of the longitudinal nonhomogeneites of the field sweep rate on the current distribution in a Rutherford type of cable can not be avoided in accelerator magnets.
the super coupling currents are not a problem for the accelerator operation, but a problem for magnet design.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nonhomogeneity in the field sweep dB/dt along a Rutherford cable can be described by super coupling currents (or SCCs) that can flow over lengths far larger that the cable pitch and which can be characterised with a characteristic time and a characteristic velocity.
a nonhomogeneous field sweep can not always be avoided in accelerator magnets and therefore a nonhomogeneous distribution of the current during a field ramp is unavoidable.
